setting: Battle of Berestechko, Volhynia, early July 1651, the last day: after the Crimean khan Islam Giray betrayed the Cossacks and carried off Hetman Khmelnytsky, the Ukrainian army retreats across the swampy Plyashivka river. Three hundred Pereiaslav regiment veterans stay behind as a rearguard in the abandoned camp: earthen trenches (shantsi) of black peat dug in soft marshy ground, a triangular redoubt jutting out from the camp, overturned wagons and torn tents, a small oak-and-alder grove (lisok) behind the camp, and beyond it the fords: open brown water about a hundred paces wide through endless bulrush and reed marsh, with brushwood and plank causeways. The crown army (Polish infantry, German mercenaries, artillery with field guns and a mortar) attacks from noon to evening. Hot summer sun, heavy white gunpowder smoke. Optional branch: a small flat-bottomed wooden boat on the open water near the ford. Epilogue: the Batih campaign a year later (1652).

characters.ivan: Ivan Hladky, a 46-year-old Pereiaslav Cossack veteran, lean weathered sunburnt face, deep-set grey eyes, short pale scar across the bridge of his nose, shaved head with a long greying-black forelock tucked behind the left ear, long drooping dark mustache streaked with grey, no beard, wiry strong build, off-white linen shirt, dark blue wool sharovary, wide crimson sash, scuffed brown leather boots, curved shablia, cow-horn powder flask, a very long heavy German arquebus with a dark walnut stock
characters.dzhalai: Dzhalai, a 42-year-old Crimean Tatar warrior, broad high-cheekboned face, narrow dark eyes, thin black mustache and a short sparse chin beard, shaved head under a black sheepskin cap, stocky muscular build, faded ochre quilted kaftan belted with leather, loose dark brown trousers tucked into soft leather boots, a short composite recurve bow, a leather quiver of fletched arrows on his hip, curved sabre
characters.fedir_bezruchko: Fedir Bezruchko, a 52-year-old Cossack veteran, broad red sunburnt face, bulbous nose, bushy grey eyebrows, shaved head with a thick white forelock, very long white mustache, heavy barrel-chested build, dark green wool zhupan with sleeves rolled up over a sweat-stained linen shirt, red sharovary, black sash, yellow leather boots, a long-handled iron chekan war hammer
characters.borodavko: Sotnyk Fedir Borodavko, a 55-year-old Pereiaslav Cossack captain, gaunt hawk-nosed face with deep wrinkles, piercing pale blue eyes, shaved head with a long grey forelock, grey mustache hanging to the collarbone, tall sinewy build, crimson kuntush over a dark blue zhupan, black-and-gold sash, red leather boots, an iron pernach mace in his sash, shablia, a short signal carbine slung across his back
characters.dmytro: Dmytro, a 30-year-old Cossack, lean hollow-cheeked face, dark forelock, black drooping mustache, sweat-soaked linen shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbow, brown zhupan, blue sharovary, green sash, a long knife in his hand
characters.cossack_veterans: the three hundred Pereiaslav Cossack veterans: grizzled men of 40 to 60, shaved heads with grey and black forelocks or fur-trimmed kalpaks, long drooping mustaches, old scars, patched zhupans in faded red, green and brown over linen shirts, wide sashes, samopal muskets, bows and quivers, sabres, powder horns, spears; no horses, no cannons
characters.polish_zholniry: Polish crown infantry (zholniry) of 1651: weathered mustached men in knee-length blue wool haiduk coats with red facings and tall felt caps, matchlock muskets, short sabres and berdysh axes, pikemen in grey coats with long pikes, dismounted dragoons in buff coats; no winged hussars
characters.german_mercenaries: German mercenary musketeers in Polish service: bearded men in steel morion and cabasset helmets, grey and buff wool coats, bandoliers of wooden powder chargers, long rifled and matchlock muskets
characters.german_officer: a German mercenary officer, about 40, ruddy face with a trimmed brown beard and upturned mustache, polished steel morion helmet, buff leather coat with a red silk sash, steel gorget, holding a nadziak war hammer
characters.polish_gunners: Polish artillery crew: men in shirtsleeves, leather aprons and felt caps, with rammers, sponges and smoking linstocks, bronze field guns and a squat bronze mortar on wooden carriages, powder kegs
characters.bykiv_riders: Cossack horsemen of the Bykiv sotnia: sunburnt mustached men in brown and grey zhupans and fur-trimmed kalpaks, pistols in their sashes, each holding the reins of a string of five saddled small steppe horses
characters.szlachcic_envoy: a Polish nobleman envoy, about 35, head shaved high at the sides with a short tuft on top, curled brown mustache, red fur-trimmed kontusz over a yellow silk zupan, karabela sabre at his hip
characters.kobzar: an old blind kobzar, about 70, long white hair and white beard, clouded eyes, plain grey woollen svyta with a leather belt, playing a pear-shaped many-stringed kobza

palette: Passages: monochrome sepia/graphite on ivory paper. Cover: original full-color photographic palette.
notes: Story text is extremely violent (throat cutting, impalement, severed heads, mortar wounds, a chain shot). Per the tone rules every such moment is shown only by implication: smoke, flashes, fallen figures at a distance, reactions, still bodies covered by coats, a figure lying face-down in water. Never depict severed heads, impalement, wounds or blood. Ivan and Dzhalai strip to the waist while digging (r/22-23); Ivan then wears the muddy crimson zhupan of a dead Polish noble while playing dead on the parapet (r/33-48). Ivan's long heavy arquebus was taken from a German at Kodak. Weapons are matchlock/wheel-lock samopals, bows, sabres, spears, chekan war hammers, hand-thrown iron grenades with fuses, stick signal rockets. Polish cavalry not used (ground too soft); no winged hussars. Dmytro appears only in the first image. Kobzar appears only in the final ballad image.
cover_palette: muted olive-green and ochre bulrushes, peat-black and brown mud, grey-white gunpowder smoke, pale hazy summer sky; accents of crimson sashes and Polish blue coats; morning scenes cool and hazy, noon harsh and bleached, late afternoon amber, evening and sunset rose-gold, the epilogue and ballad in blue pre-dawn mist
illustration_notes: Westerveld-inspired original drawings, static ink reveal, no ambient distortion. References establish medium and protagonist identity only. Preserve branch-specific costume, injuries and survivors. Full-color ultra-realistic photographic cover.
